verified_script.event: Army QB Cale Hellums converted fourth-and-1 with a 41-yard touchdown run on opening drive
verified_script.causal: Explosive rushing score and short-yardage fourth-down choice jointly

verified_script.event: Army sustained 15-play 75-yard 9:51 touchdown drive with fourth-down conversions
verified_script.causal: Rushing chain and possession clock coupling

verified_script.event: Godspower Nwawuihe 66-yard rushing TD on two-play drive
verified_script.causal: Same rush-heavy opponent mismatch generates short-clock explosive high tail

verified_script.event: Tulsa scored three unanswered touchdowns from 28-14 deficit to 35-28 lead
verified_script.causal: Tulsa explosive pass/rush capability and Army serial three-and-outs; not captured by a stable rushing-control bonus

verified_script.event: Tulsa missed a 40-yard field goal; a Tulsa 18-yard TD pass was negated by holding on that drive
verified_script.causal: Scoring finishing + discipline variance, actual missed kick

verified_script.event: Army recovered a blocked Tulsa punt at Tulsa 13 at 3:52; Army scored on five-play 13-yard drive
verified_script.causal: Non-scoring special teams flip generated a short-field offensive TD; NOT a ST touchdown

verified_script.event: Army received punt at own 37 with 51 seconds remaining; QB runs advanced ball; Jones 50-yard field goal at expiration
verified_script.causal: Last-second clock, short-yardage rushing, 50-plus-yard kick variance

failure_analysis.evidence: 73 actual points vs Build16 51.371; both teams exceeded forecast by approximately 10.8 points, while Army margin error only 0.103
failure_analysis.lesson: Separate ATS relative-margin calibration from shared offensive scoring and same-game high-total tail; do not force a postgame points offset

failure_analysis.evidence: Army 3/4 fourth downs including two Hellums fourth-and-1 TD rushes; Army third down 5/14
failure_analysis.lesson: Simulate conversion decisions conditioned on short yardage and score and time rather than using only average chain PPD

failure_analysis.evidence: Tim Kloska blocked and recovered punt at Tulsa 13, Army offense subsequently scored 7 points
failure_analysis.lesson: Model punt block/recovery as rare source-verified transition into next actual short-field possession. Do not create defensive TD, ST TD, or duplicate ordinary opportunity

failure_analysis.evidence: Army 15-play 9:51 TD and 2-play 66-yard rushing TD within same game; four consecutive Army three-and-outs in second half
failure_analysis.lesson: Within-game regime/script distribution must allow productive control, short explosive drives, and correlated temporary stalls

failure_analysis.evidence: Army made 51, 34, 50 yd FGs; Tulsa missed 40 yd try
failure_analysis.lesson: Keep attempts conditional on distance and miss probability; no deterministic reproduction of observed perfect kicker

failure_analysis.evidence: Army rushed 51/275 and Tulsa 26/148; Army +3 margin against +2.897 Build16
failure_analysis.lesson: Retain opponent-adjusted rushing advantage; avoid altering margin means based solely on total miss

forward_research_priority.target: Use raw punt_blocked / is_blocked_punt_turnover and next-drive start field position, conditional only on verified previous games; treat as alternative transition not extra score
Fit down/distance and short-yardage fourth-down choice/success to previously observed games, guard against double counting third-down/rush EPA
Quantify high-total script mass and scoring opportunity correlation via paired 5000-draw study without motivating fixture leakage
Maintain realistic source-backed 40/50+ distance misses even after this game's unusual kicking results

note: No causal decomposition of every point is identified by a single final score. Blocked punt materially changed field position; its exact marginal point value cannot be identified from actual scoring alone.
